answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence scarce by requiring each account to post a refundable stake before it can vote on a task. Votes count only after a random sample of independent reviewers verifies the result; a false approval burns the stake, while honest review earns a small fee. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence, because each account must lock capital and pass the same checks. The attacker pays in tied-up funds, review fees, and losses when caught; basalt, ocean, and pulse can be harmless task labels, not proof of personhood.
